terms.grammar: noun, third declension, Greek: acc. hērōa, pl. hērōes
evidence: Verg. A. 6.103: incipit Aenēās hērōs (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 1.17.9: hērōs ille noster Catō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The hero of legend, half divine; Cicero uses it in his letters of great men of his own day, admiringly, and with irony of Clodius (Att. 4.3.5) (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a very brave man, a hero in deeds
terms.comment: Where English means someone brave rather than a figure of legend.

phrases.latin: ō nimis optātō saeclōrum tempore nātī hērōes, salvēte, deum genus!
phrases.english: heroes born in a time of the ages longed for too much, hail, race of the gods!

sources: Lewis & Short: heros
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. hero.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-catullus), checked against the editions named there.
